# Project Atlas — Autonomous Environmental Monitoring Rover

> **SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE — NOT A REAL PROJECT.**
> Every date, measurement, component, price, person, organization and event in this
> directory is fictional and exists only to test the BuildVault Skill.
> Do not treat anything here as real project data.

## Initial proposal (original scope baseline)

- Project name: Atlas Rover
- Purpose: an autonomous ground rover that monitors environmental conditions along a
  fixed 1 km route and returns to a docking station.
- Prepared by: A. Rivera, Atlas Rover Team (fictional)
- Date: 2025-03-10
- Funding target: under 4,500 credits (fictional currency)

## Documented objectives

1. Measure air temperature and relative humidity along the route at 1 minute intervals.
2. Navigate the 1 km route autonomously and return to the docking station.
3. Log all measurements to an on-board SD card for later retrieval.
4. Allow an operator to upload waypoints from a laptop over a cable.
5. Survive light rain and dust at the two prototype sites.

## Version 1 scope (original, as documented on 2025-03-10)

- Four-wheel skid-steer chassis with independently driven wheels.
- Minimum 8 hours of operation on one battery charge.
- Temperature and relative humidity sensing.
- Waypoint upload over a cable connection.
- SD-card data logging at 1 Hz.
- Ingress protection rated IP54.
- Total vehicle mass under 6 kg.

## Explicitly deferred in version 1 (as documented on 2025-03-10)

- Live telemetry. Deferred to version 2.
- Obstacle avoidance. Deferred to version 2.
- Air-quality (particulate) sensing. Deferred to version 2.

## Known open questions at proposal time

- Number of prototype sites was not settled (one, two or three candidates).
- Whether a battery warmer is required was not evaluated.
- No measurement of motor temperature had been taken.
